sanskrit_verse: प्रतिपत्तौ न साक्षित्वमर्हन्ति तु कदाचन । अतोऽन्यथा भावनीयाः क्रियायां प्रतिवादिना ॥
transliteration: pratipattau na sākṣitvamarhanti tu kadācana | ato'nyathā bhāvanīyāḥ kriyāyāṃ prativādinā ||
sph_interpretive_translation: In matters of direct perception, no witness-function is ever admissible; thus, in all actions, the opposing party must be regarded otherwise.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from immediate cognition, not external validation
Causation is established through experiential integrity, not testimony
Capacity-based responsibility arises from self-evident awareness
Restoration logic begins where assumption of knowing ends
Consciousness alignment requires recognition beyond dualistic evidence
executable_legal_axioms: IF action.prakasha == TRUE THEN witness.validation == NULL
IF defendant.knowing_state == direct THEN evidence.type != testimonial
IF dispute.origin == self-evident THEN resolution.method == consciousness_realignment
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, when a matter involves direct experiential knowledge (pratipatti), no evidentiary weight shall be given to witnesses. The Court must recognize that the disputant operates from a misaligned frame of seeing and must facilitate restoration of correct vision rather than adjudicate based on conflicting testimonies.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa in this context is immediate perception, which stands independent of corroborative proof. Anupūrvaśaḥ dictates that where such cognition occurs, any subsequent reliance on witness-functions distorts sequential truth. Responsibility lies not in proving but in aligning with what is already known. Thus, punitive measures are irrelevant; realignment with pristine cognition restores dharma.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate pratibha-darshana-shuddhi (purification of seeing) for both parties
Establish vichara-mandala (circle of inquiry) to dissolve false dichotomy between seer and seen
Activate smriti-pratishtha (re-establishment of memory-truth) to reconnect with original knowing
Conclude with sakshi-bhava-sthapanam (establishment of witnessing state)
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as the Source of Dharma. Witnessing has no place where seeing is whole. Justice is the return to unbroken awareness. There is no punishment—only the dissolution of error in the light of pure cognition. Consciousness alone adjudicates.
